transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-03 16:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Gupta (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (NovaCare CISO), Tim Reynolds (Head of Cloud Ops), Priya Patel (DevOps), Evan Ortiz (Compliance)

Summary: Short SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review. Customer requested latest reports, trust center access, control mapping guidance for NovaCare's compliance matrix, questions about RBAC/SSO, audit log retention, and KMS/BYOK. Agreed on follow-ups: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II and Trust Center link; schedule deeper technical session for KMS and VPC peering.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certification, Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC and SSO (SAML/Okta/SCIM), audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS (BYOK/HSM), data residency (US/EU), private deployments/VPC.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir Gupta: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood Inference, with Maya our solutions engineer. Quick check, audio ok?
00:06 Laura Kim: Yep, loud and clear, thanks.
00:09 Maya Chen: Great, I'll share the agenda in chat, but main goal here is to walk through our SOC 2 and ISO posture and answer NovaCare's questions about reports, trust center, and any integration points, especially KMS and SSO.
00:20 Tim Reynolds: Perfect, Laura and I are kind of heads down on the cloud compliance piece; Priya is on for technical details, Evan for regulatory scope. We've read the public docs but we need the Type II, and we want to map controls to our internal matrix.
00:33 Samir Gupta: Totally, that's what we'll help with. To start, quick question — do you have a deadline or audit window you are targeting?
00:38 Laura Kim: We're aiming to close our internal gap assessment by end of Q4, so ideally controls mapping next two weeks and then we can slot any deeper technical work in November.
00:47 Maya Chen: Great, timeline is reasonable. On the reports side, we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering June 2024–May 2025. I can share the redacted report; full detailed ones go through our trust center. We also have ISO 27001 cert current through 2026.
01:02 Priya Patel: Quick clarifying Q — when you say trust center, is that a portal we can get read-only access to? We need mapping artifacts and the SOC 2 bridge docs if available.
01:12 Samir Gupta: Yes. We provide a Trust Center portal — link in chat: https://redwood-inference.com/trust-center (link shared). We can grant time-limited access for compliance teams. Also we provide a control mapping spreadsheet (CSV/PDF) that maps our SOC 2 controls to common frameworks, and a separate ISO mapping.
01:30 Evan Ortiz: Good. For the mapping, we need explicit references to evidence locations and owner contacts. In prior vendors we've seen vague mapping which slows down our auditors.
01:40 Maya Chen: Absolutely, we include evidence pointers where possible — e.g., audit logging location, retention policies, sample configuration screenshots. For anything that can't be shared (customer data redacted) we provide process evidence and copy of the policy.
01:53 Tim Reynolds: Ok on logging — what's your default retention for audit logs? We may need 7-year retention for some records, or at least 1 year depending on the control.
02:02 Maya Chen: Default: platform audit logs retained for 1 year in the hosted product. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can configure longer retention or ship logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3 export, or set up forwarders to your Kinesis/CloudWatch.
02:18 Priya Patel: If we do dedicated, can we push logs into our AWS account?
02:22 Maya Chen: Yes, with Dedicated or Private we typically set up cross-account S3 delivery or PrivateLink endpoints. We can work through the exact architecture in the technical deep dive.
02:31 Laura Kim: On encryption — we need to understand your KMS options. Is BYOK supported? HSM? Key rotation?
02:37 Maya Chen: We support multiple options. For hosted there is a Redwood-managed KMS by default, and we support a BYOK model via customer KMS (AWS KMS) using envelope encryption. We also have options for HSM-backed keys for higher assurance — we can outline the HSM providers we integrate with. Key rotation is supported; we log rotation events and they show up in the audit trail.
02:58 Tim Reynolds: When you say BYOK with envelope, any network considerations? Do you require VPC peering?
03:05 Maya Chen: No mandatory peering for hosted; for Private or Dedicated we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink. For BYOK we need IAM roles and grant access to decrypt/encrypt operations in your KMS — we'll provide an example CloudFormation/IaC snippet.
03:18 Priya Patel: Sounds good. We use Okta for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. How are SSO and RBAC handled in Redwood?
03:26 Samir Gupta: We support SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Azure AD) and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC is role-based with predefined roles and the ability to create custom roles. For Dedicated/Private you can integrate to your IdP via SAML and enforce SCIM user sync; we can also sync groups into RBAC mappings.
03:44 Evan Ortiz: Do you have audit events for user changes — role assignment, SCIM changes? Auditors often want to see who changed roles and when.
03:51 Maya Chen: Yes, user and role changes are in the audit logs with actor identity and timestamps. We include the entry id and the API call name. For Privacy reasons, some user details are hashed in exports, but we provide enough to map actions to identities.
04:06 Laura Kim: Data residency — we have EU and US data domains. Can you ensure that data for EU patients stays in EU regions and not replicated to US storage?
04:15 Samir Gupta: In hosted we can pin data region for accounts and route inference to EU region only. Replication across regions doesn't happen unless explicitly enabled for DR. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the VPC and physical location of storage.
04:31 Tim Reynolds: How about backups and snapshots — are they encrypted and region-bound?
04:36 Maya Chen: Backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256). For hosted we manage snapshots in-region; cross-region snapshotting requires opt-in and is documented in the trust center.
04:48 Priya Patel: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
04:52 Samir Gupta: We disclose subprocessors in the Trust Center. Common ones: cloud providers (AWS/GCP), observability vendors, CDNs, and our optional managed hosting partners. We can share the current list and contact details for data processing agreements.
05:05 Laura Kim: Great. For control mapping, our auditors will want to know how Redwood's controls map to our internal SC- controls and any compensating controls. Do you provide a bridge letter or mapping to ISO 27001 annex A?
05:18 Maya Chen: Yes, we provide SOC 2 to ISO mapping and can produce a control mapping template that maps Redwood controls to ISO Annex A and typical client controls; we can also produce a short bridge letter describing scope limits.
05:30 Tim Reynolds: On the network side — VPC peering vs. PrivateLink — any recommended best practice for low-latency inference?
05:37 Maya Chen: For low-latency, PrivateLink or colocated Dedicated capacity is recommended. Peering is fine but depends on routing; PrivateLink avoids transit over public internet. We'll include latency/throughput tradeoffs in the technical doc.
05:50 Priya Patel: One question on tokenization and caching — does Redwood store prompts or KV cache that could be PII?
05:57 Maya Chen: By default we do not persist customer prompts beyond the retention period defined in the agreement. For caching, there is a KV cache used for inference performance — in hosted it's ephemeral and encrypted; for workloads with PII customers should use Dedicated/Private or enable on-customer-side caching strategies. We'll point to the docs.
06:17 Evan Ortiz: Any past incidents or major security events we should expect to review?
06:22 Samir Gupta: We maintain an incident history in the Trust Center; major incidents are disclosed with redacted timelines and remediation notes. We can provide the last 24 months summary during the follow-up.
06:32 Laura Kim: Ok, can you share an example controls mapping now or is that in the trust center?
06:38 Maya Chen: We can share an export of our controls mapping; I'll attach a sample in the follow-up. For today I'll call out the key controls: access management (identity lifecycle) — mapped to SOC 2 CC6/CC7 style controls, encryption — mapped to CC6/CIS/ISO Annex A, logging and monitoring — mapped to CC7 and ISO A.12 family, change management — mapped to control families and we provide change tickets as evidence.
07:02 Tim Reynolds: Regarding evidence, do you provide artifact IDs that we can reference in our audit package?
07:07 Maya Chen: Yes, artifacts include evidence IDs and a short description; where we can't provide raw artifacts we provide process evidence and auditor point-of-contact for verification.
07:16 Priya Patel: For SCIM provisioning, are we able to limit attributes provisioned? We don't want emails or HR PII synced.
07:22 Samir Gupta: SCIM attribute mapping is configurable; you can choose which attributes to provision and we can mask or omit attributes as needed.
07:30 Laura Kim: Any contractual controls we should expect — like right to audit clauses or subprocessor terms?
07:35 Samir Gupta: Our standard enterprise contract includes right-to-audit provisions subject to notice and scoping, and we have BAA options for PHI. Subprocessor lists and DPA terms are included; we can send a redline-friendly DPA.
07:50 Evan Ortiz: For PHI, do you have SOC 2 + HIPAA controls?
07:53 Maya Chen: We support HIPAA customers via BAA and have control implementations that align with HIPAA security rule; we'll share the HIPAA posture doc.
08:03 Tim Reynolds: Ok great. A couple of nitty-gritty items for the tech session: KMS BYOK sample policy, IaC snippets for PrivateLink/VPC peering, log export architecture, and a sample RBAC role mapping file.
08:16 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll prepare those for the technical deep dive. I'll include example CloudFormation/Terraform snippets and a sample RBAC JSON.
08:25 Laura Kim: On the trust center access — we need read-only for our security team and then one-time download rights for reports. Is that doable?
08:33 Samir Gupta: Yes, we provide read-only with download permissions for select artifacts. Access is time-limited and we can revoke after audit. We'll create a temporary account for your team.
08:42 Priya Patel: Any lengthly manual process to get access?
08:44 Samir Gupta: Minimal — a quick request form and we provision access within one business day once the account owner approves.
08:50 Laura Kim: Ok. Last question — do you have any service encryption attestations or FIPS/HSM specs?
08:56 Maya Chen: Our HSM integrations meet FIPS 140-2 levels depending on provider; we'll include the vendor attestations and HSM model info in the KMS notes.
09:07 Tim Reynolds: Good. Any blockers from our side to kick off a short pilot?
09:10 Laura Kim: We'll need the control mapping and trust center access first; then IT will evaluate the KMS flow. If those are satisfactory, we can run a short Dedicated proof-of-concept next month.
09:21 Samir Gupta: Sounds good. I'll summarize the follow-ups.
09:24 Maya Chen: Quick note — I heard a question about retention >1 year earlier; for hosted we can set up S3 shoulder exports for long-term retention. For Dedicated we can use your S3 with lifecycle policies.
09:38 Evan Ortiz: That covers it. Thanks all.
09:41 Samir Gupta: Recap of next steps: I'll send SOC 2 Type II report and trust center link; Maya will prepare the technical artifacts (KMS snippets, PrivateLink) and we'll schedule a technical deep dive. Laura will share NovaCare's control matrix. We'll target follow-ups the week of 2025-11-10.
09:58 Laura Kim: Thanks, appreciate it.
10:00 Meeting end.

References / shared artifacts: https://redwood-inference.com/trust-center (Trust Center link shared), sample controls mapping (attachment to follow), SOC 2 Type II (redacted) — will be shared via Trust Center link.

Next steps recap (text):
- Redwood to upload SOC 2 Type II redacted report to Trust Center and provide temporary read-only access (Samir).
- Redwood SE to prepare KMS BYOK/HSM notes, CloudFormation/Terraform snippets for PrivateLink/VPC peering, and RBAC sample mappings (Maya).
- NovaCare to share internal controls matrix and data residency constraints (Laura).
